list.title: Library
list.lede: Sources, quotes and their authors — one place for every reference. You write texts in the Scriptorium and arrange knowledge (comments, people, places, events) in Knowledge; both cite from here. Everything is encrypted in the browser. Every area has its library: the area's members see it, and when the area is public — everyone. You work with all of them at once: references and search reach every library you can see.
list.name: Name
list.onlyMeNew: Only me (a private area will be created)
list.sharedHint: A shared library is read and added to by everyone who has the area's key. Every area has one library.

sealed.one: {count} entry is sealed with a key you do not have.
sealed.other: {count} entries are sealed with a key you do not have.

home.oldWhere: Texts, deliveries and projects are now in the Scriptorium; comments are a kind in Knowledge.

kindList.musicHint: Pieces, sheet music and recordings — also recordings in voices (soprano, alto, tenor, bass, instruments) that sound together. The type decides which fields an entry has; files are encrypted in the browser.

settings.area: Area: {area} — whoever has its key reads this library.
settings.areaReadOnly: Area: {area} — whoever has its key reads this library. You can only read it.
settings.seenBy: Seen by: {who}. To make an entry public (or stop it being public), move it to another area's library — on the entry, in the “Who sees it” box.

oldCopies.other: {count} entries still have old, separately published copies (from before 22.10.2026). Nobody reads them any more; they can be withdrawn.

settings.deleteHint: Deletes all entries; pages that showed them will say the text is gone. This cannot be undone. Export first (Import / export).

settle.before: This collection was made before the rule “whoever sees the area sees it”, so today nobody outside the area reads it.

settle.notPublic: The area is not public: after confirming, nothing changes for anyone outside the area.
settle.understood: I understand who will see it

json.lead: All entries (or chosen kinds) as one document — a backup, a move, work with AI. The import changes existing entries in place and adds new ones; it deletes nothing.
json.leadKind: {kind} as JSON — e.g. several books at once prepared by AI. The import also accepts the people and sources they point to; it changes existing entries in place and deletes nothing.
json.readOnly: You can only read in this library.

markup.infoTitle: Reports a source: points to a work, quote or person from the Library and does not rest on another statement.
markup.interpTitle: Your own thought, a comparison or synthesis — rests on another statement or points to no source.
markup.noThesis: No thesis: the content does not start with a sentence

area.waiting: the area's members — the area is public, but the library awaits confirmation in Settings
area.keyTaken: There the key “{from}” was already taken — the entry now has the key “{key}”. The old one stays with the entry, and texts point to it by a fixed link, so nothing broke.
area.moveLedeScriptorium: The entry keeps its id — references and embeds keep working. Those who see that scriptorium will see it. This is how a text becomes public: in the scriptorium of a public area.
area.moveLedeLibrary: The entry keeps its id — references and embeds keep working. Those who see that place will see it.
area.withType: Also move the text type “{name}” — without it, readers of that scriptorium will not see this type's fields (other texts of this type keep using it).
area.files: The files ({n}) go together with the entry — encrypted with that area's key; this may take a moment.
area.refsWarn: Whoever sees only one of the libraries will see “{unreadable}” in place of a reference — without title or content.

key.pinned: Texts that named the entry by its old key ({n}) now point to it permanently.
key.pinnedSome: Texts that named the entry by its old key ({n}) now point to it permanently; {failed} in libraries you cannot change — there the old key, kept with the entry, works.
key.title: Citation key
key.hint: In a text: [@{key}] or [@{key}, s. 12] — a fixed link is saved, so changing the key breaks nothing.
key.taken: Another entry in this library already has this key — a letter will be added.
key.elsewhere: An entry in another library you can see already has this key. Writing [@{key}] in this library chooses this entry; texts save a fixed link, so nothing gets mixed up.
key.wrong: Only letters, digits and the signs . _ : -
